title: Approvals — quorum, per-group sign-off (会签), inbox

items.title: Per-group sign-off (会签) needs one approval from EACH group
personas: approver holding exactly one group (e.g. manager)
second approver holding the other group (e.g. finance/auditor)

requires: a launched per_group request whose two groups resolve to two DISTINCT users (showcase: ExpenseSignoffFlow on EXP-2001, Ada Auditor holds auditor — seeded since #3409)

steps: as the single-group approver, open the request in the approval inbox
record the pending slate and per-group progress from the drawer
approve, then re-read the request state over the API

acceptance.clause: one group's approval satisfies that group and drops it from the pending slate, but the request stays pending on the remaining group
acceptance.verify: before: status=pending, both groups 0/1; after the approve: status STILL pending, approver's group satisfied, other group's user still listed as pending
acceptance.evidence: before/after API reads of the request (status + pending approvers)

acceptance.clause: per-group progress is server-computed, not a client guess
acceptance.verify: the drawer renders per-group tick badges ('N of M groups', group chips with counts) that match the API state
acceptance.evidence: drawer screenshot alongside the API read

negative: contrast case: a request whose slots all resolve to ONE user finalizes on a single decision — confirm per_group did NOT (that contrast is the proof the behavior differs)

history.change: initial import from the #3358 evidence run (decisive oracle: group drops but request stays pending)

items.title: M-of-N quorum approves at the threshold; one rejection vetoes
personas: three DISTINCT users each holding one of the approver positions

requires: a quorum (minApprovals: 2) request whose three position approvers resolve to three distinct users
knownGaps: showcase admin holds manager+finance+legal, so the slate collapses to one person and the runtime clamps 2-of-3 to 1-of-1 — M-of-N is not demonstrable on stock seeds (#3358); needs a dedicated fixture or seed change

blocked.ref: #3358 (quorum slate collapses onto the admin — showcase design call pending)

steps: as approver 1, approve — confirm the request stays pending (1 of 2)
as approver 2, approve — confirm the request finalizes and remaining tasks close
on a second request: as any approver, reject — confirm immediate veto

acceptance.clause: the request approves exactly when minApprovals distinct approvals are recorded
acceptance.verify: status transitions pending→pending→approved across the two approvals; approval action rows count 2 distinct actors

acceptance.clause: a single rejection vetoes even with quorum-1 approvals already recorded
acceptance.verify: status flips to rejected on the first reject; no further tasks remain actionable

history.change: initial import from #3358; carried the fixture blocker forward explicitly

items.title: Inbox actions are metadata-driven and gated by the viewer's relationship
personas: approver who is NOT the submitter
same user viewing a request they submitted

requires: requests with a real (non-null) submitter — seeded since #3411 (invoice submitted by admin, others by a no-position persona)

steps: as the same viewer, open one request submitted by someone else and one they submitted themselves
record the rendered action set on each

acceptance.clause: approver-side actions (approve/reject/reassign/send-back/request-info) render from declared metadata on the other-submitter request
acceptance.verify: after confirming render via screenshot, read the action buttons from the drawer DOM and match the declared action set

acceptance.clause: submitter-side actions (send-reminder, recall) appear ONLY on the viewer's own request
acceptance.verify: own-request drawer shows the two extra actions; other-submitter drawer does not
acceptance.evidence: side-by-side action lists for the two requests

acceptance.clause: each action executes its REST route (spot-check one: the decision commits)
acceptance.verify: clicking an action issues its API call and the state change round-trips
acceptance.evidence: network trace of the action call

history.change: initial import from the #3358 evidence run (7-action table proven after #3411 stamped real submitters)

items.title: A submitter who is not an approver sees no approver buttons
personas: submitter holding NO approver position on their own pending request

requires: one pending request routed to a position its submitter does not hold
knownGaps: stock seeds route every request to positions the admin holds, so the admin is an approver on all of them (#3358) — needs one request addressed away from the signed-in persona

blocked.ref: #3358 (needs a request routed to a position the viewing submitter does not hold)

steps: sign in as the no-position submitter
open their own pending request from the '我发起的' tab

acceptance.clause: approve/reject buttons do not render for the submitter, and the gate is server-side, not a client heuristic
acceptance.verify: the drawer omits approver actions AND a forged direct POST of the decision route as the submitter is rejected (test both sides of the gate)
acceptance.evidence: screenshot of the drawer + the rejected API call

source: ADR-0057 D10 (server is the authoritative visibility gate)

history.change: initial import from #3358; upgraded the oracle from DOM-only to both-sides (UI absence + server rejection)

items.title: An approval notification deep-links straight into the request drawer
steps: click an approval bell notification (or open the ?request=<id> URL it carries) on a fresh page load

acceptance.clause: the ?request= URL opens the request drawer directly on a cold load
acceptance.verify: fresh navigation to .../approvals?request=<id> renders the drawer for that exact request (verify twice on fresh loads)

history.change: initial import from #3358 (verified twice on fresh loads)
